messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: continuous-batcher pod gpux-03.runtime-prod crashed (OOM) x3 in 2m; high queue depth observed. Host: us-west-2a. Auto-escalating to oncall.

alice (oncall): saw alert, looking. any customer-facing issues yet?

ben (eng-runtime): logs show CUDA OOM inside batcher process, then container crashloop. stack traces point at kv_prefetch.lua allocation spike. suspect prefetch + runaway batch growth.

carla (eng-sre): adding metrics: queue_length jumped from ~200 to 18k over ~7m, memory per-pod climbed to 46GB then OOM on 48GB instance. Paging pressure also high (swap thrash).

alice (oncall): noted. will start mitigation steps. david, if you're free pls take handoff in 15m?

elaine (support): support reports 6 customers with intermittent 503s and high token latency (5-30s) starting ~16:02 UTC. one large customer reported a spike in failed requests to embeddings route.

frank (customer-success): pinged the top two affected accounts, letting them know we're investigating. they'll expect an ETA.

ben (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: continuous-batcher has a regression under specific seq-length distribution where shard accumulator doesn't release memory fast enough; combined with KV-prefetch aggressive prefetch count it keeps growing. when node flap happens (we saw gpux-03 losing PCI bus briefly at 16:04), processes requeued requests to same pods and growth snowballed.

carla (eng-sre): agree. immediate mitigation options: 1) disable kv-prefetch at runtime for batchers 2) reduce BATCHER_MAX_BATCH_SIZE / BATCHER_MAX_SHARD_SIZE 3) cordon+drain gpux-03 and recycle, 4) scale up cluster (short term).

alice (oncall): doing 1 + 2 now. applying env overrides to stop prefetch and cap shards. deploy-bot, please apply the config change to runtime namespace.

deploy-bot: executing: `kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/continuous-batcher KV_PREFETCH_ENABLED=false BATCHER_MAX_SHARD_SIZE=64` — rolling restart will happen.

ben (eng-runtime): also pushing a hotfix to limiter logic in a patch branch but won't be ready for minutes. for now disabling prefetch should prevent runaway mem usage.

carla (eng-sre): while that's rolling, i'm going to cordon gpux-03 and drain the remaining runtime pods off it. command: `kubectl cordon gpux-03 && kubectl drain gpux-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

alice (oncall): executing drain now. notifying infra to watch for node-level flaps.

deploy-bot: rollout status: continuous-batcher updated (env var change) — 6/8 pods restarted, new pods report RSS ~= 9.2GB.

carla (eng-sre): nice. memory per pod trending down. queue length down to ~3k and falling. paging I/O reduced.

david (oncall): i'm taking over the thread from alice (she needs to triage an unrelated pager). handoff notes: prefetch disabled, shard cap 64 applied, gpux-03 drained, support notified. i'll coordinate postmortem owner.

elaine (support): escalation update: affected customers were notified at 16:20 UTC. support will keep the ticket open for 24h and update if any regressions after rollout.

frank (customer-success): customers asked for postmortem; please assign owner. i'll coordinate comms.

ben (eng-runtime): patch queued: PR #4522 adds a guard to the shard accumulator and improves prefetch backpressure. target merge in 45m, will require a careful canary.

carla (eng-sre): short-term follow-up: keep prefetch off for 2h, monitor mem + queue. if stable, we can re-enable with lower prefetch limits and the patch. also recommending an autoscale rule: if queue_length > 5k then scale continuous-batcher replicas by +2.

alice (oncall): note: the kernel OOM logs referenced `oom_reaper` and `cuda:oom` in dmesg. infra to check driver stability on gpux-03.

infra-ops (via carla): driver reloaded on gpux-03, no hardware errors found; we suspect transient PCI glitch. node remains cordoned pending monitoring.

deploy-bot: PR #4522 merged to canary branch. initiating canary rollout to 2 pods in us-west-2.

ben (eng-runtime): canary logs look good: accumulator usage bounded, memory stable ~8-10GB. will promote after 30m of stable metrics.

david (oncall): customer impact summary for incident record: ~6 customers affected, partial 503s and latency spikes 16:02-16:25 UTC, degradation largely resolved by config rollback (prefetch off) and node drain. severity: SEV2.

carla (eng-sre): assigning postmortem: ben (eng-runtime) to own technical write-up, carla to own mitigation timeline, elaine to own customer timeline. action items: 1) add accumulator guard (PR done), 2) add circuit-breaker to prefetch, 3) autoscale rule by queue_length, 4) add node pci/fabric monitoring alert.

ben (eng-runtime): ack. i'll open the postmortem draft and include the hotfix checklist + revert plan.

frank (customer-success): i'll draft customer-facing summary once postmortem has initial notes.

alice (oncall): closing active pager for now — monitoring for 1h. handing full follow-up to david. thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident auto-note: Pager closed by alice at 16:32 UTC. Create incident record ID: INC-2026-173555.

carla (eng-sre): leaving monitoring alarms set; will escalate if queue starts trending back up.

ben (eng-runtime): final note — root trigger looks like combo of transient node error causing requeue + a latent growth bug in the accumulator. will prioritize test-case that simulates requeue during high-prefetch to avoid regression.
